newsitem.title: USA: Daedalus has loss, auditors concerned.
newsitem.headline: Daedalus has loss, auditors concerned.

text.p: Daedalus Enterprises Inc said Tuesday it incurred a loss for its fiscal 1996 year and its auditors have raised doubts about the ability of the company to continue operating.

Daedalus, which develops and makes remote sensing instruments for environmental measurements and monitoring, reported a loss for its fiscal year ended July 31, 1996 of $967,000 or $1.85 a share on revenues of $2.1 million.

Daedalus said that an independent auditor's report on the company's financial statements for its fiscal 1996 year by Deloitte & Touche LLP included a paragraph which said the company's cash flow difficulties raise substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern.

Daedalus said it signed a new secured line of credit agreement with its bank which is due on demand. It said it believes that its increased backlog and improving business prospects and new line of credit will permit it to recover from recent difficulties and generate sufficient cash flow to sustain its operations.
Daedalus' fiscal 1996 results compare with a loss of $362,000 or $0.70 a share and revenues of $3,624,000 for the preceding year.

Daedalus also said its backlog at the end of fiscal 1996 was about $1,014,000 compared with about $574,000 at the end of fiscal 1995. In addition, Daedalus said it received a large international standard product order for $1,189,000 during the first quarter of fiscal 1997.

Daedalus said it was negotiating for several standard product orders which the company hopes to receive in the current fiscal year and expects to capture a significant NASA product development contract by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 1997. Management is hopeful that such orders will be received although no assurances can be given, it said.

Last December, Daedalus suspended payment of its semi-annual dividend to allocate more financial resources to its growth plan. The plan, implemented in fiscal 1995, was not expected to impact materially on revenues until late in fiscal 1996, the company had said at the time.
